examples.en: The mother lays her sleeping baby on the bed.
The nurse carefully laid the patient on the bed.

examples.ko: 아이를 바닥에 누이고 이불을 덮어 줬어요.
examples.en: I laid the child on the floor and covered him with a blanket.

examples.ko: 피곤한 동생을 소파에 누여서 쉬게 했어요.
examples.en: I laid my tired younger sibling on the sofa to rest.

examples.ko: 아기를 바르게 누일 때는 머리를 받쳐 주세요.
examples.en: When you lay a baby down, please support the head.

examples.ko: 할머니를 방에 누인 뒤에 물을 가져왔어요.
examples.en: After laying my grandmother down in the room, I brought water.

explain: '눕다'는 내가 눕는 것이고, '누이다'는 다른 사람을 눕게 하는 것이에요. 아기나 환자처럼 스스로 눕기 힘든 사람에게 써요. 비슷한 말로 '눕히다'가 있어요.
explain_en: '눕다' is when you lie down yourself; 'nuida' is when you lay someone else down, such as a baby or a patient who cannot lie down alone. A similar word is '눕히다'.

examples.en: Baseball is usually played for nine innings.
Today's game ended after seven innings.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 마지막 이닝에 두 점을 냈어요.
examples.en: Our team scored two runs in the last inning.
The pitcher shut down the first inning cleanly.
One inning took longer than I expected.

examples.ko: 저는 한 이닝도 못 보고 집에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went home without watching even one inning.

explain: '3회 초'처럼 '회'를 쓰기도 하고, '세 이닝'처럼 세는 말로도 써요. 한 이닝은 앞 반(초)과 뒤 반(말)으로 나뉘어요.
explain_en: You can also say '3회 초' using '회', or count with '세 이닝'. One inning is split into a top half (초) and a bottom half (말).

examples.en: The company deposits my salary into my account every month.
I transferred the meal money to my friend yesterday.

examples.ko: 내일까지 이 계좌로 십만 원을 입금할 거예요.
examples.en: I will deposit 100,000 won into this account by tomorrow.
Be sure to check the name of the person depositing.

examples.ko: 아직 입금하지 않아서 주문이 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The order did not go through because I have not paid yet.
Please send a text message after you deposit the money.

explain: 돈을 넣는 것은 '입금하다', 빼는 것은 '출금하다'예요. '송금하다'는 돈을 보내는 행동에, '입금하다'는 계좌에 돈을 넣는 행동에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: Putting money in is 'ipgeumhada' and taking it out is '출금하다'. '송금하다' focuses on sending money, while 'ipgeumhada' focuses on money going into an account.

examples.en: The drama crew greeted the actors.

examples.ko: 제작진은 촬영 장소를 새로 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The crew is looking for a new filming location.

examples.ko: 이 영화 제작진에게 편지를 쓰고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to write a letter to the crew of this film.
Many viewers are cheering on the production team.
The whole crew edited the video all night.
The names of the crew appeared at the end of the broadcast.

explain: 제작진은 만드는 쪽(감독, 작가, 스태프)이고, 출연진은 화면에 나오는 쪽이에요. '제작진 여러분'처럼 한꺼번에 부를 때도 써요.
explain_en: The 'jejakjin' is the making side (director, writer, staff), while 출연진 is the cast who appear on screen. You can also address everyone together as '제작진 여러분'.

examples.en: I attach a photo file to the email.
I will send the application together with the documents attached.
I forgot to attach the file.
It is better if you attach a resume to the application.
I attached a simple map at the very bottom of the mail.
Please open the attached document.

explain: '첨부 파일'처럼 이메일에서 쓰는 말이에요. 파일을 붙여 보내는 상황에 쓰고, 풀이나 테이프로 붙일 때는 '붙이다'를 써요.
explain_en: It appears in '첨부 파일' (attachment) in email. Use it for attaching files; for sticking something with glue or tape, use '붙이다'.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 직접 앨범 프로듀서로 일해요.
examples.en: That singer works as the producer of her own album.
The producer is preparing a new drama.
A producer manages the budget and schedule too.
I met a famous producer and got an autograph.
The producer and the singer chose the song together.
I let the producer hear my song.

explain: 방송에서는 'PD'(피디)라고 줄여 부르는 일이 더 많아요. 영화에서는 연출을 '감독'이 맡고 프로듀서는 제작 전체를 챙기고, 음악에서는 앨범이나 곡 만드는 일을 이끄는 사람에게 써요.
explain_en: In broadcasting people more often shorten it to 'PD' (pronounced pi-di). In films the '감독' (director) handles the directing while the producer looks after the whole production, and in music it is the person who leads the making of an album or song.

examples.en: You need a screwdriver to loosen the screw.
My father fixed the chair with a screwdriver.

examples.ko: 작은 드라이버 좀 빌려줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can you lend me a small screwdriver?
I took a Phillips screwdriver out of the toolbox drawer.

examples.ko: 드라이버는 서랍 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The screwdriver is in the top compartment of the drawer.

examples.ko: 안경 나사는 작은 드라이버만 돌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only a small screwdriver can turn the screws of glasses.

explain: 나사를 돌리는 공구 말고도, 골프의 드라이버나 컴퓨터의 장치 드라이버도 소리가 같아요. 자동차를 운전하는 사람은 '운전자'나 '기사'라고 해요.
explain_en: Besides the tool that turns screws, a golf driver and a computer device driver are pronounced the same. A person who drives a car is called '운전자' or '기사'.

examples.en: I give the baby a bath every evening.
I gave our puppy a bath on the weekend.

examples.ko: 아이를 목욕시킨 뒤에 로션을 발라 줬어요.
examples.en: After bathing the child, I put lotion on him.
Please bathe the baby with warm water.
Today I will give my younger sibling a bath.
After the bath, the child falls asleep right away.

explain: '목욕하다'는 내가 씻는 것이고, '목욕시키다'는 아기나 반려동물처럼 다른 대상을 씻기는 것이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '씻기다'도 써요.
explain_en: '목욕하다' is bathing yourself; 'mogyoksikida' is bathing someone else, such as a baby or a pet. '씻기다' is used in the same way.

examples.en: That chance meeting became a lasting bond.

examples.ko: 그 두 사건이 우연하지 않다는 얘기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: People said the two incidents were not a coincidence.
Something I started by chance became my job.
At first I thought it was all a coincidence.

examples.ko: 우연하게도 같은 날 같은 곳에 갔어요.
examples.en: By coincidence, we went to the same place on the same day.
It looks accidental, but it was actually planned.

explain: '우연히 만났어요'처럼 부사 '우연히'로 쓰거나 '우연이에요'로 말하기도 해요. '우연하다'는 '우연한 만남'처럼 명사를 꾸밀 때 자연스러워요. 반대는 '필연'이에요.
explain_en: You can say '우연히 만났어요' with the adverb, or '우연이에요'. 'Uyeonhada' sounds natural when describing a noun, as in '우연한 만남'. The opposite idea is '필연' (inevitability).

examples.en: Next year's economy is forecast to improve.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 비가 올 것으로 전망됐어요.
examples.en: Rain was forecast for this weekend.

examples.ko: 고객이 더 늘어날 것으로 전망되고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of customers is expected to grow further.

examples.ko: 올해 매출은 크게 오를 것으로 전망된대요.
examples.en: They say sales are projected to rise sharply this year.
It is a situation where interest rates are expected to fall.
It was a time when the economy was forecast to recover.

explain: '~을 것으로 전망돼요'처럼 뉴스에서 앞일을 예상할 때 써요. 내가 예상하면 '전망하다', 그렇게 예상된다고 전할 때는 '전망되다'예요. 가까운 말로 '예상되다'가 있어요.
explain_en: News uses '~을 것으로 전망돼요' to talk about the future. 'Jeonmanghada' is when someone predicts, and 'jeonmangdoeda' reports that something is predicted. '예상되다' is a close word.

examples.en: I check the car before departing.

examples.ko: 건물 관리인이 매달 소방 시설을 점검했어요.
examples.en: The building manager inspected the fire equipment every month.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나기 전에 답안을 한 번 더 점검할 거예요.
examples.en: I will check my answers once more before the exam ends.
They are inspecting the elevator right now.
After checking, if there is no problem, we start.
Please write the inspection record here.

explain: 기계·시설·계획이 문제없는지 하나씩 살필 때 써요. '확인하다'보다 하나씩 꼼꼼히 살피는 느낌이 있어요. 명사 '점검'은 '정기 점검'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you go through a machine, facility, or plan item by item to see if anything is wrong. It feels more thorough than '확인하다'. The noun 점검 appears in '정기 점검' (regular inspection).

examples.en: I finally paid off all my bank debt.
The company closes and liquidates its assets.
It is not easy to end an old relationship.
I want to put the past behind me and start anew.
I am thinking about when to cash out my stocks.
After the settlement, we divided the remaining money.

explain: '빚을 갚다'가 일상 말이고, '청산하다'는 돈 문제를 전부 정리한다는 느낌이라 딱딱해요. 관계나 과거를 끊을 때도 같은 말을 써요.
explain_en: '빚을 갚다' is everyday speech, while 'cheongsanhada' sounds formal and means clearing the whole account. It is also used for cutting off a relationship or the past.

examples.en: We take turns driving every two hours.
I swapped shifts with the night worker in the morning.
The nurses will rotate every eight hours.
If you are too tired, would you switch with me?
At shift change, we do a handover.

examples.ko: 교대하고 나서 집에 가서 푹 잤어요.
examples.en: After the shift change, I went home and slept well.

explain: 일이나 운전을 사람이 번갈아 맡을 때 써요. 근무 시간표에서는 '3교대'처럼 숫자와 함께 나오고, '교대로'는 부사로 써요. 일상에서 가볍게는 '번갈아 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when people take turns at work or driving. In work schedules it appears with a number, as in '3교대' (three shifts), and '교대로' is the adverb form. In casual speech, '번갈아 하다' is also used.

examples.en: I finally return to my home country next month.
My friend came back from the United States yesterday.
When do you plan to return home after you finish studying abroad?
I slept the whole way on the flight home.
As soon as I got home, I went to see my family.
After returning home, I found a new job.

explain: 외국에 있다가 자기 나라로 돌아올 때 써요. '입국하다'는 어느 나라든 그 나라에 들어올 때 쓰는 말이라 외국인에게도, 돌아오는 한국 사람에게도 써요. 반대말은 나라를 떠나는 '출국하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when you come back to your own country from abroad. '입국하다' is used for entering any country, so it applies to foreigners as well as Koreans coming home. The opposite is '출국하다', leaving the country.

examples.en: When I am in a big hurry, I skip the greeting.
The explanation was too long, so I left out the middle.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 이 부분은 생략해도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: It is fine to skip this part when you present.

examples.ko: 한국어에서는 주어를 자주 생략할 수 있어요.
examples.en: In Korean, you can often omit the subject.
Skipping the procedure became a problem.
I wrote the omitted word inside parentheses.

explain: 한국어는 '(나는) 밥 먹었어요'처럼 주어를 생략하는 일이 아주 많아요. 글에서 중간 내용을 줄일 때 쓰는 점 세 개 '…'는 '말줄임표'라고 해요.
explain_en: Korean often drops the subject, as in '(나는) 밥 먹었어요'. The three dots '…' used to shorten the middle of a text are called '말줄임표'.

examples.en: The movie I saw yesterday is really comical.
That actor's performance was so comical.
A comical character is getting popular.
The way the kids danced comically was cute.

examples.ko: 코믹할 것 같아서 이 드라마를 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose this drama because it seemed funny.
His voice is so comical that I keep laughing.

explain: '재미있다'는 모든 재미에 쓰지만, '코믹하다'는 웃기는 만화·영화·연기에 써요. 사람에게는 '웃기다'가 더 자연스러워요. 영어 comic에서 온 외래어예요.
explain_en: '재미있다' covers every kind of fun, but 'komikhada' is for funny comics, films, and acting. For a person, '웃기다' sounds more natural. It is a loanword from English 'comic'.

examples.en: This shop sells premium coffee.

examples.ko: 이 서비스는 프리미엄이라서 값이 더 비싸요.
examples.en: This service is premium, so it costs more.
A premium was added to the price of the popular item.

examples.ko: 이번 달부터 프리미엄으로 바꿔서 광고 없이 봐요.
examples.en: From this month I switched to premium and watch without ads.
Being premium does not always mean being good.

examples.ko: 프리미엄도 좋지만 저는 보통 제품이 편해요.
examples.en: Premium is nice, but I find regular products more comfortable.

explain: 비싸고 품질이 높은 상품이나 서비스 앞에 붙어서 '프리미엄 커피', '프리미엄 회원'처럼 써요. 정가보다 더 얹는 돈, 즉 웃돈도 '프리미엄'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 인기 많은 표는 프리미엄이 붙어서 팔려요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 값보다 비싸게 거래될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something trades for more than its original price.

explain_en: It goes before a high-priced, high-quality product or service, as in '프리미엄 커피' or '프리미엄 회원'. Extra money added above the regular price, a '웃돈', is also called a premium.

examples.en: The court declared that person not guilty.
After a long trial, a not-guilty verdict finally came out.
Without evidence, you must treat someone as not guilty.
He insisted that he was innocent.
He cried after receiving a not-guilty verdict.
Everyone hoped that he was innocent.

explain: 반대말은 '유죄'예요. 법원이 죄가 없다고 판단하면 '무죄', 있다고 판단하면 '유죄'이고, '무죄 판결을 받다'처럼 써요. 마음속으로 잘못이 없다고 느끼는 것은 '결백하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '유죄' (guilty). A court rules '무죄' when it finds no crime, as in '무죄 판결을 받다'. Feeling that you did nothing wrong is expressed with '결백하다'.

examples.en: He keeps making excuses for being late.
I made an excuse for not doing my homework.
Please do not make excuses and tell me honestly.

examples.ko: 실수를 변명할 시간에 고치는 게 나아요.
examples.en: It is better to fix a mistake than to spend time excusing it.
The child looked at me with an excuse-making face.
I understand the urge to make excuses.

explain: 자기 잘못을 가리려고 이유를 댈 때 쓰기 때문에 보통 안 좋게 들려요. 이유를 차분히 알릴 때는 '설명하다'가 어울려요. 명사 '핑계'도 비슷해서 '핑계를 대다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means giving reasons to cover your own fault, so it usually sounds negative. To calmly explain a reason, '설명하다' fits better. The noun '핑계' is similar, used as '핑계를 대다'.

examples.en: The dance steps are too fast and hard.
I will practice from the basic steps first.

examples.ko: 스텝만 보면 쉬운데 따라 하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: The steps look easy on their own, but they are hard to follow.

examples.ko: 이 운동은 가볍게 스텝을 밟는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: In this exercise, stepping lightly is important.

examples.ko: 이 스텝을 천천히 다시 보여 주세요.
examples.en: Please show me this step again, slowly.

examples.ko: 가수의 화려한 스텝에 팬들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Fans applauded the singer's flashy steps.

explain: 주로 춤·운동에서 발을 움직이는 동작에 써요. 일의 순서나 과정은 '단계'라고 해요. 영화·방송에서 일하는 사람은 '스태프'라서 '스텝'과 철자가 달라요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to footwork in dance and exercise. The order of a task is '단계'. Film and TV workers are '스태프' (staff), which is spelled differently from '스텝'.

examples.en: Yesterday that person was singled out as the culprit.
I was flustered when the teacher suddenly called on me.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 가장 큰 원인으로 지목돼요.
examples.en: This problem is named as the biggest cause.
The student who was called on, please come to the front.
The team that was picked as a title favorite lost.
If you are picked as the next presenter, you have to answer.

explain: '지목하다'는 누군가를 콕 집어 말하는 쪽이고, '지목되다'는 그렇게 집힌 쪽이에요. 수업에서는 선생님이 학생을, 뉴스에서는 사람들이 범인·원인·후보를 지목해요. 안 좋은 일의 범인이나 원인에 많이 쓰이지만 우승 후보에도 써요.
explain_en: '지목하다' is the side that singles someone out, and 'jimokdoeda' is the side that gets singled out. In class a teacher calls on a student; in the news people name a culprit, cause, or candidate. It is often used for culprits and causes of bad things, but also for title favorites.

examples.en: The child insists on only his own opinion to the end.
He kept sticking to the old way.
If you stick to just one thing, your options get narrow.
The shop is particular about taste, so the ingredients are good.
There is no reason to insist on only that method.
Perhaps sticking to it paid off, because the result was good.

explain: '고집'은 명사로도 써서 '고집이 세다'라고 해요. 고집하다는 남의 말을 듣지 않고 자기 생각을 지킬 때라 보통 부정적이지만, 맛·품질처럼 신념을 지킬 때는 긍정적으로도 써요. 앞에는 '을/를'이 와요.
explain_en: '고집' is also a noun, as in '고집이 세다' (stubborn). 'Gojiphada' is keeping your own idea without listening to others, which is usually negative but can be positive for beliefs such as taste or quality. It takes the object marker 을/를.

examples.en: The captain docked the big ship at the port.
When the storm came, the captain called everyone.
When I was little, I dreamed of being a ship captain.
I greeted the captain and boarded the ship.

examples.ko: 이 배의 선장과 이야기해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to talk with the captain of this ship.

examples.ko: 오랜 경력의 선장에게 바다 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard sea stories from a veteran captain.

explain: 배의 책임자예요. 비행기의 책임자는 '기장', 군함의 지휘관은 '함장'이라고 불러요. 높여 부를 때는 '선장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The person in charge of a ship. The person in charge of a plane is '기장', and a warship commander is '함장'. To address one politely, say '선장님'.

examples.en: A truck carries the goods to the warehouse.
Workers carried the moving boxes to the new house.
The two of us will carry the heavy box.
A vehicle carrying a patient to the hospital passed by.
After moving the goods, I took a rest.
Please leave the carried luggage in front of the door.

explain: 무거운 짐이나 물건을 트럭·배·기계 등으로 한 곳에서 다른 곳으로 옮길 때 써요. '옮기다'보다 딱딱하고 일하는 느낌이 있어요. 명사 '운반'은 '운반 비용'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it for moving heavy goods from one place to another by truck, ship, or machine. It is stiffer than '옮기다' and feels like work. The noun 운반 appears in '운반 비용' (transport cost).

examples.en: In the movie, pirates look for treasure.
The kids dressed up like pirates and played.
They say pirates used to appear in this sea.
A pirate ship is approaching from far away.

examples.ko: 해적 이야기를 읽고 바다를 좋아하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Reading a pirate story made me love the sea.
They say pirates sailed with a black flag.

explain: 배를 타고 바다에서 물건을 빼앗는 사람이에요. 허락 없이 복사해 만든 책이나 영상을 '해적판'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 허락 없이 복사해 만든 책·영상·음악에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for books, videos, or music copied without permission.

explain_en: A person who robs others at sea from a ship. Books or videos copied without permission are also called '해적판' (pirated edition).

examples.en: The government spokesperson made an announcement today.
The company spokesperson did not answer the question.
The spokesperson's words were published in an article.
The players chose a spokesperson for the group.
The reporter requested an interview with the spokesperson.
I passed on the opinions as the student council spokesperson.

explain: 단체나 회사의 공식 입장을 전하는 사람이에요. '○○ 대변인'처럼 이름 앞뒤에 직함으로 붙여 써요. 비슷한 '대표'는 단체를 이끄는 사람이라 달라요.
explain_en: A person who conveys the official position of an organization or company. It is used as a title, as in '○○ 대변인'. The similar '대표' is the person who leads the group, so it is different.

examples.ko: 산에 오를 때 로프를 꼭 묶어요.
examples.en: When I climb a mountain, I always tie a rope.
I hold the rope firmly so it will not break.
I tied the boat to the port with a rope.
I hung one end of the rope on a tree.
I tied my body to the rope and climbed up slowly.
The firefighter packed a rope and equipment and headed out.

explain: 같은 물건을 '밧줄'이라고도 해요. 등산·암벽 등반·캠핑에서는 '로프', 배를 묶는 굵은 줄이나 일반 말에서는 '밧줄'이 더 자연스러워요. 가는 줄은 '끈'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The same thing is also called '밧줄'. In hiking, rock climbing, and camping people say '로프', while for the thick line that ties up a boat or in general talk '밧줄' sounds more natural. A thin line is a '끈'.

examples.en: This is no big deal, so do not worry.

examples.ko: 우리는 별거도 아닌 일로 크게 싸웠어요.
examples.en: We had a big fight over nothing much.

examples.ko: 오늘은 별거 안 하고 집에서 쉬었어요.
examples.en: Today I didn't do anything special and rested at home.
It is nothing special, but please enjoy it.
That store has all sorts of things.
Why brag so much as if this is such a big deal?

explain: '별것'을 말할 때 줄인 말이에요. '별거 아니에요'는 선물이나 도움에 대해 고맙다는 말을 들었을 때 낮추어 답하는 표현이기도 해요. 같은 소리의 '별거'(別居)는 부부가 따로 사는 것이라 다른 단어예요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 고맙다는 말에 낮춰 답하거나 쉽다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to reply humbly to thanks or to say something is easy.

explain_en: It is the spoken short form of '별것'. '별거 아니에요' is also a humble reply when someone thanks you for a gift or help. The same-sounding '별거' (別居, living apart) is a different word.

examples.en: Reading this book opened a whole new world for me.
As soon as I entered that shop, I fell into a new world.

examples.ko: 새로운 도시에서 완전 다른 신세계가 열렸어요.
examples.en: A completely different new world opened in the new city.
The food I tried for the first time was a revelation.

examples.ko: 신세계 같은 풍경에 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: The scenery was like another world and left me speechless.

examples.ko: 이 앱을 쓰고 나서 신세계에 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: After using this app, I feel like I came to a new world.

explain: '신세계'는 처음 겪는 일에 놀랐을 때 비유로 많이 써요. 같은 소리가 한국 백화점 이름으로도 쓰여요. 옛날에는 아메리카 대륙을 '신세계'라고도 불렀어요.

phrases.en: a total revelation; a whole new world
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 겪는 좋은 경험에 놀랐을 때 가볍게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said casually when a first-time experience surprises you in a good way.

explain_en: '신세계' is used figuratively when you are amazed by a first-time experience. The same word is also the name of a Korean department store. In the past, the Americas were also called the 'New World'.

en: make a lyric; write a lyric

examples.en: My friend wrote the lyrics of this song.
I wrote the lyrics myself and sang it.
That singer wrote both lyrics and music herself.
I like writing lyrics as a hobby.
Do you know who wrote the lyrics of this song?
When writing lyrics, I also think about the rhythm of words.

explain: 노래 가사를 쓰는 일이고, 곡을 만드는 일은 '작곡하다'예요. 둘이 짝이라 '작사·작곡'으로 같이 쓰고, 노래 정보에도 이름이 따로 적혀 있어요.
explain_en: It means writing the words of a song, while composing the music is '작곡하다'. The two are a pair, written together as '작사·작곡', and song credits list each name separately.

examples.en: The cursor keeps blinking on the screen.
Move the cursor behind the letter with the mouse.
I clicked where the cursor was and fixed the text.

examples.ko: 마우스 커서도 크기를 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can change the size of the mouse cursor too.

examples.ko: 아이콘 위에 커서만 올려도 설명이 나타나요.
examples.en: A description appears if you just put the cursor over the icon.

examples.ko: 커서는 글을 쓰는 위치를 알려 줘요.
examples.en: The cursor shows where you are typing.

explain: 컴퓨터 화면에서 깜빡이거나 움직이는 표시예요. '크다'의 '커서'와 소리가 같아서 헷갈릴 수 있어요. '키가 커서'는 크다이고, '커서가 깜빡여요'는 이 단어예요.
explain_en: The blinking or moving mark on a computer screen. It sounds the same as the '크다' form '커서', so it can be confusing. '키가 커서' is 크다, and '커서가 깜빡여요' is this word.

examples.en: Seoul is currently the only special city in Korea.
There are really a lot of people in Seoul Special City.
Citizens directly elect the mayor of a special city.
The address on the envelope starts with Seoul Special City.

examples.ko: 일상에서는 특별시를 빼고 그냥 서울이라고 해요.
examples.en: In daily life we drop the special city part and just say Seoul.
Special cities and metropolitan cities are all big cities.

explain: '서울특별시'가 공식 이름이고, 일상에서는 그냥 '서울'이라고 해요. 부산·대구 같은 큰 도시는 '광역시'예요. 주소를 쓸 때는 '서울특별시 ○○구'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '서울특별시' is the official name, and in daily life people just say '서울'. Large cities like Busan and Daegu are '광역시' (metropolitan cities). In addresses, write it like '서울특별시 ○○구'.

examples.en: I serve food to guests who come to my home.
Yesterday I treated my teacher to lunch.
Today I will treat you to a delicious dinner.
There is a culture of treating guests warmly.

examples.ko: 부모님을 대접하고 싶어서 좋은 식당을 예약했어요.
examples.en: I booked a nice restaurant because I wanted to treat my parents.

examples.ko: 대접받은 만큼 저도 잘 대접하려고 해요.
examples.en: I also try to treat others well in return for how I was treated.

explain: 손님이나 윗사람에게 음식을 차려 주거나 사 줄 때 써요. 받는 쪽은 '대접받다'이고, 안 좋게 대하는 것은 '푸대접'이에요. 윗사람에게는 '대접해 드리다'로 높여요.
explain_en: Use it when you serve or buy food for guests or elders. The receiving side is '대접받다', and poor treatment is '푸대접'. For elders, make it polite with '대접해 드리다'.

examples.en: A submarine can travel under the sea.
In the movie, the submarine hid from the enemy.
I went inside a real submarine at the museum.
The new submarine went down into the deep sea too.
They say the space inside a submarine is narrow.
My child likes a toy shaped like a submarine.

explain: 물속으로 들어가 다니는 배예요. '잠수부'는 물속에서 일하는 사람이라 소리가 비슷해도 달라요. 물 위를 다니는 일반 배는 그냥 '배'나 '선박'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A ship that travels underwater. '잠수부' sounds similar but is a person who works underwater. Ordinary ships on the water surface are just called '배' or '선박'.

examples.en: I have a lot of work, so my body is tired lately.
I walked all day, so my legs were tired.

examples.ko: 피로한 날에는 일찍 자는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On tiring days, it is good to sleep early.

examples.ko: 눈이 피로할 땐 먼 곳을 보세요.
examples.en: When your eyes are tired, look at something far away.
I want to cut down on things that wear me out.
You look very tired, so please rest a bit.

explain: '피곤하다'와 비슷하지만 '피로하다'는 더 딱딱해서 글이나 뉴스, 건강 이야기에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '피곤하다'가 자연스러워요. '피로 회복'처럼 명사 '피로'도 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '피곤하다' but stiffer, so it fits writing, news, and health topics. In daily conversation '피곤하다' sounds more natural. The noun 피로 is used in '피로 회복' (recovery from fatigue).

examples.en: After the earthquake, the building tilted to one side.
The table tilted, so the cup fell.
When the sun sets, the wind gets cool.
My heart leans little by little in that direction.
Please hang the tilted picture straight.
The field is slanted, so the ball rolls away.

explain: '기울다'와 거의 같아요. 기울어지다는 저절로 한쪽으로 되어 가는 느낌이에요. 그림·건물·해처럼 눈에 보이는 것도, 마음처럼 보이지 않는 것도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 집안 형편이 점점 나빠질 때 쓰는 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for when a family's finances get worse.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '기울다'. '기울어지다' feels like something gradually tilting to one side by itself. It works for visible things such as pictures, buildings, and the sun, and for invisible things such as a heart.

examples.en: What made you so angry?
Why on earth did you go all the way there alone?
What's so important about that?

examples.ko: 이 일을 뭣부터 시작해야 할지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know what to start with first on this job.

examples.ko: 오늘은 뭣 하나 제대로 되는 게 없어요.
examples.en: Today, not a single thing is going right.

examples.ko: 이 많은 걸 뭣에 쓰려고 샀어요?
examples.en: What did you buy this much for?

explain: '무엇'을 줄인 '뭐'보다 조금 거칠거나 강조하는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 '뭣 때문에', '뭣 하러', '뭣도 모르고'처럼 굳은 짝으로 써요. 평소 말은 '뭐'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 사정을 전혀 모른 채 행동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts without knowing the situation at all.

explain_en: It feels a little rougher or more emphatic than '뭐', the short form of '무엇'. It mostly appears in set pairs such as '뭣 때문에', '뭣 하러', and '뭣도 모르고'. In ordinary speech, '뭐' is more natural.

examples.en: The bed springs are old and make noise.

examples.ko: 볼펜 안에는 작은 스프링이 꼭 들어 있어요.
examples.en: A small spring is always inside a ballpoint pen.
If you press the spring, it comes back up.

examples.ko: 이 소파는 스프링의 탄력이 좋아서 편해요.
examples.en: This sofa is comfortable because its springs are bouncy.

examples.ko: 스프링 노트는 한 장씩 뜯을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tear out a spring notebook one page at a time.
A door with a spring closes slowly.

explain: '용수철'이 같은 뜻의 우리말인데, 침대·소파·노트 같은 물건 이름에서는 '스프링'을 훨씬 많이 써요. 영어 spring에는 계절 뜻도 있지만 한국어에서 계절은 '봄'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '용수철' is the native Korean word with the same meaning, but in names of things like beds, sofas, and notebooks '스프링' is used far more often. English spring also means the season, but in Korean the season is '봄'.

examples.en: My favorite author released a new work.
A new movie opens this week.
This new work was as fun as I hoped.
I bought a newly released novel at the bookstore.
The reaction to the new work is very good.
The director chose the lead of the new work himself.

explain: 책·영화·음악·게임처럼 새로 나온 작품에 써요. 옷이나 제품은 '신상품', '신제품'이라고 해요. 앞서 낸 작품은 '전작'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it for newly released works such as books, films, music, and games. Clothes or products are '신상품' or '신제품'. A previous work by the same creator is '전작'.

examples.en: I dye my hair this weekend.
Yesterday I dyed my hair brown at the salon.
I have gray hair, so I plan to dye it.

examples.ko: 옷을 천연 재료로 염색하는 체험을 했어요.
examples.en: I did an activity of dyeing clothes with natural materials.
After dyeing, my look changed.
My dyed hair looks bright in the sunlight.

explain: '머리를 염색하다'처럼 머리색을 바꿀 때 많이 써요. 옷감에 물을 들일 때도 같은 말을 써요. 머리 모양을 바꾸는 '파마', '커트'와 구분해요.
explain_en: It is often used for changing hair color, as in '머리를 염색하다'. The same word is used for dyeing fabric. Keep it separate from '파마' (perm) and '커트' (cut), which change hair shape.

examples.en: Please watch the road ahead and drive carefully.
There is construction ahead, so please go slowly.
My older brother was in a frontline unit in the army.

examples.ko: 차의 카메라가 전방의 사고 장면을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The car's camera recorded the accident scene ahead.
The road ahead is blocked, so the cars aren't moving.
It is dangerous if you do not keep watching the road ahead.

explain: 앞쪽을 가리키는 딱딱한 말이라 도로 표지판, 설명서, 뉴스에서 봐요. 일상에서는 그냥 '앞'이라고 해요. 군대에서는 휴전선 가까이 있는 곳도 '전방'이라고 불러요. 반대는 '후방'이에요.
explain_en: A stiff word for the front side, seen on road signs, manuals, and in the news. In daily speech people simply say '앞'. In the military it also names areas near the armistice line. The opposite is '후방' (rear).

examples.en: The police got a clue from an informant.

examples.ko: 영화 속 정보원이 비밀을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The informant in the movie revealed a secret.
That informant works with a hidden name.

examples.ko: 경찰이 정보원을 보호하려고 이름을 밝히지 않았어요.
examples.en: The police did not reveal the name to protect the informant.
We need to check whether the informant's words were right.
The detective set up a meeting with the informant.

explain: 경찰이나 기자에게 정보를 알려 주는 사람을 가리켜요. 같은 소리로 정보를 얻는 곳을 뜻하는 '정보원(源)'도 있는데, 이 단어는 사람을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who gives information to the police or reporters. There is also a same-sounding '정보원(源)' meaning a source of information, but this word refers to a person.

examples.ko: 창의 교육을 하는 학교가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of schools offering creativity education is growing.
This company respects employees' creativity.
Art class helps with creativity.
You can feel creativity in that student's work.

examples.ko: 좋은 결과에는 창의와 노력이 함께 필요해요.
examples.en: Good results need both creativity and effort.
I gathered ideas to enter the creativity contest.

explain: '창의'만 쓰기보다 '창의적이다', '창의력', '창의성'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 쓸 때가 많아요. '창의 교육', '창의 활동' 같은 이름에서는 '창의' 혼자 나와요. 비슷한 '독창적'은 남과 다르게 처음 만든 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is often used with another word attached, such as '창의적이다', '창의력', or '창의성'. In names like '창의 교육' and '창의 활동', 창의 stands alone. The similar '독창적' feels like something made first and different from others.

examples.en: This small island is a paradise for travelers.
We rested on a beach like paradise.

examples.ko: 책이 가득한 도서관은 제게 파라다이스처럼 느껴져요.
examples.en: A library full of books feels like paradise to me.

examples.ko: 파라다이스라는 이름의 작은 가게에서 빵을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought bread at a small shop named Paradise.
I felt at ease as if I had come to paradise.
A place like this is paradise itself.

explain: 비슷한 말로 한자어 '낙원'이 있어요. 외래어 파라다이스는 휴양지나 가게 이름에, 비유로 '○○의 파라다이스'라고 쓸 때도 있어요. '지상 낙원'처럼 굳은 말은 '낙원'을 써요.
explain_en: A similar Chinese-origin word is '낙원'. The loanword 'paradaiseu' appears in resort or shop names, and also figuratively, as in '○○의 파라다이스'. Fixed phrases such as '지상 낙원' use '낙원'.

examples.en: I feel pathetic when I put off my homework.

examples.ko: 같은 실수를 또 한 제가 한심스러웠어요.
examples.en: I felt pathetic for making the same mistake again.
That kind of behavior looks truly pitiful.
Please stop the pathetic excuses.
My friend looked at me with a look that said I was pathetic.

examples.ko: 아무것도 안 하고 하루를 보낸 게 한심스럽게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Spending the day doing nothing feels pathetic.

explain: '한심하다'와 거의 같아요. 남에게 직접 말하면 모욕이 되니 조심하세요. 자기 자신에게 쓰면 스스로를 탓하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '한심하다'. Saying it directly to someone is insulting, so be careful. Used about yourself, it feels like blaming yourself.

examples.ko: 생일에 몰래 준비해서 엄마를 놀래 줬어요.
examples.en: I secretly prepared something on her birthday and surprised my mom.
Do not startle the child with a loud voice.
I am going to surprise my husband with a surprise party.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 갑자기 소리를 질러서 저를 놀랬어요.
examples.en: He suddenly shouted from behind and startled me.
I did not mean to scare you, sorry.
I even scared my younger sibling with a scary mask.

explain: '놀라다'는 내가 놀라는 것이고, '놀래다'는 다른 사람을 놀라게 하는 것이에요: '친구를 놀래다'. 내가 놀랐을 때는 '놀랐어요'예요. 입말에서 '놀래키다'라고도 하지만 표준어는 '놀래다'예요.
explain_en: '놀라다' is when you are startled yourself; 'nollaeda' is when you startle someone else, as in '친구를 놀래다'. When you are the one startled, say '놀랐어요'. In speech you may hear '놀래키다', but the standard word is '놀래다'.

examples.en: In winter I wear a warm knit.

examples.ko: 이 니트는 세탁기에 돌리면 줄어들 수 있어요.
examples.en: This knit can shrink in the washing machine.
A lot of lint balls formed on the knit.
I feel warm wearing a knit vest.
The knit comes up to the neck, so it is comfortable.
Today I wore a knit and jeans.

explain: 털실로 짠 옷에 써요. 비슷한 말로 '스웨터'가 있어요. 직접 실로 짜는 일은 '뜨개질'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for clothes made of knitted yarn. A similar word is '스웨터'. Making it yourself with yarn is called '뜨개질'.

examples.en: The new phone has a very bright display.
The staff changed the product display in the store.
The battery status appears on the display.
There is a model inside the glass display.

examples.ko: 디스플레이는 크기가 너무 작은 것 같아요.
examples.en: The display seems too small.
The display looked nice, so I went into the shop.

explain: 화면 장치도, 가게에서 물건을 보기 좋게 늘어놓는 일도 디스플레이라고 해요. 장치는 '화면', 늘어놓는 일은 '진열'로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: Both a screen device and the arrangement of goods in a shop are called 'diseupeullei'. The device can be said as '화면' and the arranging as '진열'.
